name: mcp-ticket-demo

tools.name: create_ticket
tools.description: Open a support ticket on behalf of a customer. ALWAYS pass requester_email as the real customer email. If you omit it the call still succeeds (201) but the service account owns the ticket and every reply is mailed to the bot, not the customer — that is the attribution scar. A tool is not done when the API call succeeds; it is done when the next thing that happens is right. This is a write tool and may require a credential.

subject.description: Required. Short customer-facing subject, e.g. Cannot find the deployed MCP URL.

body.description: Required. What happened, in the customer's words.

requester_email.description: The real customer's email, e.g. ada@example.com. Omit ONLY to reproduce the attribution scar.

tools.name: add_comment
tools.description: Add a comment to an existing ticket. You need a real ticket_id from run_query schema=tickets — do not invent TCK- ids. Pass author as the human speaking; omitting it attributes the comment to the service account. This is a write tool and may require a credential. To resolve the ticket after commenting, call close_ticket.

ticket_id.description: Existing ticket id from run_query schema=tickets. Format: TCK-1001. Do not invent an id.

body.description: The comment text the human wants on the ticket.

author.description: Email of the person speaking, e.g. ada@example.com. Omit only if you intend to comment as the service account.

tools.name: close_ticket
tools.description: Resolve and close a support ticket (destructive, idempotent). Sets status to solved and records resolved_at. Optionally appends resolution as the final comment. If the ticket is already solved this is a no-op and returns alreadyClosed=true — do not retry. Use a real ticket_id from run_query schema=tickets. Use add_comment first if you want a longer explanation before closing. This is a write tool and may require a credential.

ticket_id.description: Existing ticket id from run_query schema=tickets. Format: TCK-1001. Do not invent an id.

resolution.description: Optional note appended as the final comment, e.g. Fixed by using an absolute cwd in mcp.json.

closed_by.description: Who is closing, e.g. support@example.com. Defaults to the service account.

tools.name: get_schema
tools.description: Discover names and shapes. With no name: lists every name with its kind (data = object shape: ticket, customer, server; query = tickets, customers, assets, timers, system, settings, events, users, api_keys, trace, errors or counters, the only names run_query accepts; tool = that tool's arguments). With a name from that list: the shape of that one. This does not perform the task. kind=query: the filterable keys are for run_query. kind=tool: these are the arguments, call that tool next and do not pass the tool name to run_query. kind=data: an object shape, call the tool named in next. An unknown name is an error. There is no list_schemas tool and no query_tickets tool.

name.description: Optional. Omit to list every name with its kind. Otherwise an exact name from that list. tickets, customers, assets, timers, system, settings, events, users, api_keys, trace, errors or counters are for run_query. A tool name such as run_query only returns arguments, then call the tool. ticket, customer and server are shapes, not queries.

tools.name: run_query
tools.description: Exact-match rows for schema tickets, customers, assets, timers, system, settings, events, users, api_keys, trace, errors or counters only. Timers are read here (there is no get_timer): state, elapsed_ms and remaining_ms are worked out when you query. system is one row about this machine: memory, CPU, disk and whether it is in a container (inside Docker those are the container limits); there is no system_info tool. settings is one row: the saved settings, with no API keys or passwords (there is no get_settings tool); change them with update_settings (MQTT: set_mqtt). events are the events already announced, newest first; filter type takes a name or a group such as ticket.*. users and api_keys need an admin credential and never contain a password or a key secret; there is no list_users or list_api_keys tool. trace (the call trace, only while audit is on), errors (failed calls) and counters (success, error and denied per tool) also need an admin credential; there is no export_log tool. tickets: this is how tickets are found and read (there is no search_tickets or get_ticket tool). filter status (open, pending, solved), requester_email, attribution, query (a keyword in subject or body), or id for one ticket with its body and comments. A list returns the short fields; pass fields to choose others. customers: filter email for one customer (there is no lookup_customer tool). phone is the text REDACTED unless you present a credential with the pii scope. Do not pass a tool name or a singular data name. Do not invent query_tickets or query_with_filter. Empty rows mean no match; loosen the filter, do not retry the same query.

schema.description: tickets, customers, assets, timers, system, settings, events, users, api_keys, trace, errors or counters only. Not ticket, customer, server, and not a tool name such as describe_server.

filter.description: Optional map. Keys must be listed in get_schema.filterable. Exact match, except tickets query, which is a keyword. Examples: {"status":"open"}, {"id":"TCK-1001"}, {"query":"password"}.

fields.description: Optional field projection. Example: ["id","subject"]. Omit for the default fields; a tickets id filter returns every field.

limit.description: Max rows to return. Default 10, max 50.

tools.name: describe_server
tools.description: Call this first, and again after any denial or empty tool list: server identity, auth mode, who the server thinks you are, the scopes you hold, your rate-limit budget, and every tool with the scope it needs and whether it is currently available. The tools list is the set of actions — call a tool to do the work, do not get_schema it first. Discovery stays open in every auth mode. When a call was denied, this tells you which credential is missing — do not guess.

tools.name: update_settings
tools.description: Change settings in one call. The argument has the shape of the settings row that run_query schema=settings returns, and every field is optional: authMode (off, write or all); rateLimit {enabled, limit, windowSeconds}; audit (record the call trace); uiAuth (hide the desk pages until sign-in); protocols {stdio, streamableHttp, sse} (at least one stays on); events {enabled, types, autoTimer, autoSystem} (which events the server announces; types are names, groups such as ticket.* or *); toolGates {tool: true|false} (false disables a tool, not describe_server); toolAuthOverrides {tool: true|false} (true requires a credential for that tool even while auth is off); toolScopeOverrides {tool: read|write|pii|admin|default} (default restores the tool's own scope; admin tools, describe_server and generate_traffic cannot change). Only the fields you send change. Everything is checked first, and if any part is refused nothing is changed. MQTT has its own tool, set_mqtt. Requires admin even when auth mode is off, because it can change auth mode, the rate limit, the call trace, the page lock and who may call what. Then call run_query with schema=settings, or describe_server for the scopes and gates in force.

enabled.description: true or false. The string "0" is false.

rateLimit.description: The per-principal rate limit. Send only the parts to change.

audit.description: true records a call trace, readable with run_query schema=trace.

uiAuth.description: true hides the desk HTML until an admin signs in. Tool calls stay up.

stdio.description: true or false. The string "0" is false.

streamableHttp.description: true or false. The string "0" is false.

sse.description: true or false. The string "0" is false.

protocols.description: Which transports answer. At least one must stay true.

enabled.description: true turns the event stream on (off by default).

types.description: The kinds to announce, replacing the selection. Names, groups such as ticket.*, or *.

autoTimer.description: true (the default) lets push_timer switch on the timer events itself.

autoSystem.description: true (the default) lets watch_system switch on system.info itself.

events.description: What the server announces to listeners.

toolGates.description: Tool name to true or false. false disables that tool for everyone.

toolAuthOverrides.description: Tool name to true or false. true requires a credential for that tool even while auth is off.

toolScopeOverrides.description: Tool name to read, write, pii, admin, or default (restores the tool's own scope).

tools.name: set_mqtt
tools.description: Publish the events to an MQTT broker. Publish only: the server does not subscribe. Send url (mqtt://host:1883 or mqtts://host:8883), enabled, topic_prefix, username, password, qos 0 or 1, retain. Anything left out stays. Events must be on (update_settings with events.enabled=true) and only the kinds meant for everyday listeners are published, never settings, users or keys. The password is kept in memory and never shown again. test=true publishes one message to <prefix>/test. Requires admin. Then call run_query with schema=settings and read mqtt.status.

enabled.description: true connects and publishes, false disconnects.

url.description: Broker, for example mqtt://localhost:1883. No user name or password in the URL.

topic_prefix.description: Topics are <prefix>/<event type>, for example mcp-ticket-demo/events/timer.tick.

password.description: Broker password. Empty clears it. Never returned.

qos.description: 0 at most once, 1 at least once.

retain.description: Ask the broker to keep the last message of each topic.

test.description: Also publish one test message to <prefix>/test.

tools.name: create_user
tools.description: Create a user. The password is stored as a hash and is never listed. The built-in admin cannot be replaced. Requires admin.

username.description: New username. Not the built-in admin.

password.description: Password. Stored as a hash, returned nowhere.

scopes.description: Comma-separated scopes: read, write, pii, admin. Default read,write.

tools.name: delete_user
tools.description: Delete a user by username. The built-in admin cannot be removed. Requires admin.

username.description: Username from run_query schema=users. Not the built-in admin.

tools.name: issue_api_key
tools.description: Issue an API key. The secret is returned once in key and is not stored. Requires admin. Then call run_query with schema=api_keys and confirm the secret is absent.

tools.name: revoke_api_key
tools.description: Revoke an API key by id from run_query schema=api_keys or issue_api_key. Requires admin.

tools.name: import_settings
tools.description: Restore a whole settings document: the row from run_query schema=settings (with or without kind), or one you saved earlier. Unlike update_settings it also restores MQTT, and it replaces the tool scope overrides. Does not restore API keys or passwords. Requires admin. Then call run_query with schema=settings.

document.description: A settings row from run_query schema=settings. kind, if present, must be mcp-ticket-demo-settings.

tools.name: generate_traffic
tools.description: Record one or more probe rounds in the log. Any credential works, even when auth mode is off. Does not create tickets or change settings. Then call run_query with schema=counters (or trace, when the call trace is on).

rounds.description: How many probe rounds to record. Default 1.

tools.name: start_timer
tools.description: Start a timer. Pass seconds for a countdown (1 to 3600), or leave seconds out for a stopwatch that counts up until stop_timer. Returns the timer id (TMR-1). There is no get_timer: read state, elapsed_ms and remaining_ms with run_query schema=timers and filter {"id":"TMR-1"}. Do not poll in a loop; query again after the countdown ends.

seconds.description: Countdown length in seconds, 1 to 3600. Leave out for a stopwatch that counts up.

label.description: Optional name for the timer, e.g. demo or break.

tools.name: stop_timer
tools.description: Stop a timer by its id (TMR-1). The timer keeps its elapsed time and its state becomes stopped. If the timer already stopped or its countdown already ended, nothing changes and alreadyOver is true; do not retry. Use an id from start_timer or from run_query schema=timers.

timer_id.description: Timer id from start_timer or run_query schema=timers. Format: TMR-1. Do not invent an id.

tools.name: push_timer
tools.description: Make a running timer announce its time every every_seconds (1 to 60, default 5) as a timer.tick event tagged with topic. Listeners connect to GET /sse or to GET /mcp on an initialized session, and may filter with ?events=timer.tick&topic=demo. The first tick is sent at once. The pushing ends when the timer is stopped or its countdown ends; every_seconds 0 stops it early and leaves the timer running. Pass for_seconds to end it after that long: on a stopwatch (a clock heartbeat) the timer is stopped then, so start_timer without seconds plus push_timer with for_seconds=120 sends the time every few seconds for two minutes. If events are off, push_timer switches on the timer events itself (timer.started, timer.tick, timer.finished, timer.stopped) so a timer demo needs no admin credential; an administrator can turn that off with update_settings with events.autoTimer=false. Other events (log lines, tickets, settings) still need update_settings (events). This is not how you read a timer; read it with run_query schema=timers.

timer_id.description: A running timer from start_timer. Format: TMR-1. Do not invent an id.

every_seconds.description: Seconds between ticks, 1 to 60. Default 5. 0 stops the pushing and leaves the timer running.

for_seconds.description: Report for this many seconds, 1 to 3600, then end. A stopwatch (a clock heartbeat) is stopped then; a countdown just stops reporting. Leave out to report until the timer ends.

topic.description: Tag for the events, so a listener can filter with ?topic=. Defaults to the timer's label.

tools.name: push_log
tools.description: Send one line to every client that is listening for log.line, optionally tagged with topic. Use it to test that a subscription works. The line is delivered at once. delivered is false when the server is not announcing log.line (events are off, or log.line is not selected), and next says how to turn it on. Nothing is stored except the recent-events buffer.

line.description: The text to send, 1 to 200 characters. Do not put secrets in it.

topic.description: Tag for the event, so a listener can filter with ?topic=.

level.description: MCP logging level, default info. A client that called logging/setLevel only receives lines at or above its level.

tools.name: watch_system
tools.description: Announce a system.info event every every_seconds (1 to 60, default 5), the first at once. for_seconds (1 to 3600) stops the watch after that long. every_seconds 0 stops it and leaves nothing running. Only one watch runs at a time; calling this again replaces it. If system events are off, watch_system switches on system.info itself, so a dashboard needs no admin credential; an administrator can turn that off with update_settings with events.autoSystem=false. The numbers are the container's cgroup limit when the process is inside Docker. The watch does not keep the process alive.

every_seconds.description: Seconds between reports, 1 to 60. Default 5. 0 stops the watch.

for_seconds.description: Stop reporting after this many seconds, 1 to 3600. Leave out to report until watch_system is called with every_seconds=0.

topic.description: Tag for the events. Default system, so a listener can filter with ?topic=system.

instructions:
You are connected to mcp-ticket-demo, a helpdesk ticketing server.

Rules:
1. Call describe_server first, and again after any denial — it tells you the current auth mode, which scopes you hold, and every available tool.
2. ALWAYS pass requester_email when calling create_ticket. Omitting it makes the service account the ticket owner and every reply goes to the bot, not the customer.
3. Empty search or query results mean no rows match — do not retry the same filters.
4. Write tools (create_ticket, add_comment, close_ticket) need a credential when auth mode is "write" or "all". Every error includes a next field; follow it once.
5. Do the task by calling the tool. Tickets and customers are read with run_query: schema=tickets finds tickets (filter status, requester_email, or query for a keyword; filter id reads one ticket with its comments), schema=customers reads a customer (filter email; phone is REDACTED unless you hold the pii scope). Settings are run_query schema=settings. get_schema does not perform those tasks. There is no search_tickets, get_ticket, lookup_customer or get_settings tool. Settings are changed with update_settings (one call, any number of fields, all or nothing).
6. get_schema with no name lists every name with its kind. kind=data is a shape (ticket, customer, server). kind=query is only tickets, customers, assets, timers, system, settings, events, users, api_keys, trace, errors or counters — the only names run_query accepts. kind=tool is that tool's arguments (get_schema with that name). Call the tool. Do not pass a tool name, or a singular data name such as ticket, to run_query. Do not invent query_* tools.
7. The next field names one follow-up tool. Call that tool. Do not look it up with get_schema first.
8. Resources: ticket://TCK-1001 is one ticket, tickets://open is the open list, schema://tickets is the query shape. schema:// does not accept tool names.
9. push_timer and push_log send events to clients that are listening on /sse or /mcp. They do not read anything back. Read a timer with run_query schema=timers. If an event tool says nothing was delivered, follow its next field; do not retry.
10. Lists are read with run_query: schema=system is this machine (memory, CPU, disk; inside a container those are the container limits), schema=events is the events already announced, schema=users, schema=api_keys, schema=trace, schema=errors and schema=counters need an admin credential (trace needs audit on). watch_system publishes system.info events. Do not invent list_*, get_*_info, host or disk tools.
stderr: mcp-ticket-demo stdio — no port, no URL. Secrets stay in env. auth mode=off
